_comment: CANONICAL MCP tool catalog. Single source of truth for BOTH paths:
mcp-hub vendors a byte-identical copy at rhorizon_mcp_hub/tools.json,
because the two packages install independently and neither may import
the other. tests/test_tool_catalog_parity.py fails the build if the two
files diverge -- they previously drifted apart unnoticed.
Descriptions are PROMPT MATERIAL: the model reads them. They must be
true on BOTH paths, so do not name a control that only one path has.
The stdio path additionally enforces a local policy.toml allow-list;
the daemon path is bounded by the agent token's scopes + namespaces.

tools.name: vault_status
tools.description: Whether the vault is sealed/unsealed. No side effects.

tools.name: vault_whoami
tools.description: Show what the calling vault token can do -- scopes, allowed namespaces, expiry. Call once to learn your boundaries before reads.

tools.name: vault_list_namespaces
tools.description: Namespaces the calling token can see. May be further narrowed by the server's local allow-list.

tools.name: vault_list_secrets
tools.description: List secret NAMES (never values) in a namespace. Restricted to what the calling token may read, and further filtered by the server's local allow-list where one is configured.

tools.name: vault_get_secret
tools.description: Read a secret value. The namespace/name must be permitted by the calling token, and by the server's local allow-list where one is configured; refused with a policy-denied error otherwise.

tools.name: vault_audit_tail
tools.description: Recent audit entries (requires audit:r on the token).

tools.name: vault_cluster_health
tools.description: Cluster and PostgreSQL HA health: overall state, readiness, and per-component state with a short reason (database, node, cluster, database_ha). Read-only summary; requires cluster:r on the token.
